detail.query: Computer Vision, Social Kinematics, 3D Scene Understanding, LLMs · VLA · Creative AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Computer Vision and Generative Intelligence (CS590-01)
교과개요
This course explores the cutting-edge intersection of computer vision, large language models (LLMs), and embodied intelligence. We move beyond traditional 2D image analysis to tackle 3D scene understanding, social kinematics in human-agent interactions, and the development of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. The curriculum integrates foundational deep learning architectures with state-of-the-art generative AI techniques, focusing on how multimodal systems perceive, reason about, and creatively generate content in complex environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design and implement robust 3D scene reconstruction pipelines, analyze dynamic social interactions using kinematic models, and fine-tune VLA agents for creative problem-solving tasks. The course aims to cultivate the ability to bridge theoretical understanding of LLMs with practical applications in robotics and generative media, fostering innovation at the frontier of artificial intelligence.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1-2: Foundations of Multimodal Learning - Bridging Vision and Language
Week 3-4: Deep Dive into Large Language Models (LLMs) and Attention Mechanisms
Week 5-6: Computer Vision Fundamentals for Generative Tasks (Diffusion Models, GANs)
Week 7-8: 3D Scene Understanding - NeRFs, Gaussian Splatting, and Point Cloud Analysis
Week 9-10: Social Kinematics - Modeling Human Motion and Interaction Dynamics
Week 11-12: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models for Embodied AI
Week 13-14: Creative AI Applications - Generative Design and Multimodal Reasoning
Week 15-16: Capstone Project - Building a Prototype VLA System for Real-world Scenarios

detail.query: Theory of Computation (Computational Geometry, Graph Theory), Security for Critical Infrastructure, ICS Security, Wireless Sensor Networks에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
이산수학 및 알고리즘 설계 (CS305-01)
교과개요
This course explores the theoretical foundations of computation with a focus on discrete structures and algorithmic efficiency. Topics include graph theory, computational geometry, complexity classes (P, NP, etc.), and formal verification techniques. The curriculum bridges abstract mathematical concepts with practical applications in network security, critical infrastructure protection, and wireless sensor networks. Students will learn to model complex systems using graphs and geometric constraints, analyze the security properties of distributed protocols, and design algorithms that are both correct and efficient for resource-constrained environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate real-world problems in terms of graphs and geometric spaces, prove the computational complexity of proposed algorithms, and apply formal methods to verify the security of critical infrastructure systems. The course also aims to develop rigorous reasoning skills for analyzing distributed network behaviors and designing robust protocols for wireless sensor networks under adversarial conditions.

---

보안 및 신뢰성 공학 (CS410-01)
교과개요
This course addresses advanced challenges in securing cyber-physical systems, specifically targeting critical infrastructure and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. Utilizing concepts from the theory of computation, we examine vulnerabilities in wireless sensor networks and industrial control systems (ICS). The course covers formal security models, intrusion detection mechanisms, and resilience strategies against physical-cyber attacks. We will analyze how computational geometry can be used for spatial access control and how graph-theoretic approaches enhance network topology protection. Practical sessions focus on simulating attacks on critical infrastructure and developing countermeasures that maintain system availability and integrity.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to identify security flaws in distributed wireless sensor networks, design resilient architectures for critical infrastructure using graph-based redundancy, and apply formal verification techniques to ensure the correctness of safety-critical algorithms. The course also aims to foster an understanding of the trade-offs between computational efficiency and security guarantees in resource-limited environments, enabling students to lead the development of trustworthy embedded systems.

detail.query: Computer Vision, Multimodal AI, Physical AI, Medical AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Physical AI for Robotics (ME450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of deep learning and physical laws to create intelligent agents that can interact safely and efficiently with the real world. Unlike traditional data-driven approaches that rely solely on massive datasets, this curriculum integrates differential equations, conservation laws, and geometric constraints directly into neural network architectures. Students will investigate how multimodal sensor inputs (vision, force, proprioception) can be fused to learn dynamic models of physical environments, enabling robust control in unstructured settings such as medical surgery or disaster response.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate physical constraints as differentiable layers within neural networks, design multimodal perception systems that align visual observations with physical dynamics, and develop simulation-to-real transfer strategies for robotic manipulation. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to critique existing AI models through the lens of physical plausibility and ethical safety in high-stakes domains like healthcare.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Physical AI - Why Physics Matters in Deep Learning
2 주차: Differentiable Physics - Embedding Conservation Laws into Neural Networks
3 주차: Multimodal Perception for Robotics - Fusing Vision, Force, and Proprioception
4 주차: Geometric Deep Learning on Manifolds for 3D Object Manipulation
5 주차: Learning Dynamics from Data - System Identification with Neural ODEs
6 주차: Simulation-to-Real Transfer - Domain Adaptation in Physical Environments
7 주차: Medical AI Applications - Robotic Surgery Planning and Tissue Deformation Modeling
8 주차: Safety-Critical Control - Lyapunov Stability Analysis for Learned Controllers
9 주차: Multimodal Foundation Models for Embodied Agents - Vision-Language-Action Integration
10 주차: Uncertainty Quantification in Physical Predictions - Bayesian Methods for Safe AI
11 주차: Case Study I - Autonomous Navigation in Cluttered Environments
12 주차: Case Study II - Assistive Robotics for Elderly Care and Medical Assistance
13 주차: Ethics and Regulation of Physical AI - Bias, Fairness, and Accountability
14 주차: Project Presentations and Final Examinations

detail.lab: 컴파일러 및 런타임 시스템 연구실(Corus Lab)
detail.query: Compiler Optimization / Homomorphic Encryption Compiler /, GPU Compiler for AI/Graph / Domain-specific Compiler에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
컴파일러 최적화 및 도메인 특화 컴파일러 (Compiler Optimization / Domain-Specific Compiler)
교과개요
This course explores the advanced techniques and architectural challenges in building high-performance compilers for modern computing platforms. We will cover the full compilation pipeline from source code to optimized machine code, with a specific focus on graph-based optimization strategies, dataflow analysis, and resource-aware scheduling. The curriculum bridges theoretical compiler design with practical implementation, addressing critical issues in parallelism extraction, memory hierarchy management, and energy efficiency. Special attention is given to emerging domains such as GPU acceleration for AI workloads, homomorphic encryption execution environments, and hardware-specific instruction set architectures (ISA). Students will learn how to construct domain-specific compilers that automatically translate high-level mathematical models into efficient low-level code tailored for heterogeneous systems.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design and implement compiler passes that effectively optimize complex computational graphs for both CPU and GPU architectures. They will gain proficiency in applying graph rewriting techniques, performing precise dataflow analysis, and managing memory layouts for large-scale matrix operations common in AI applications. Furthermore, students will develop the capability to create domain-specific intermediate representations (IR) and backend generators that support specialized hardware constraints, including those required for secure computation via homomorphic encryption. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how compiler innovations directly impact performance, scalability, and energy consumption in next-generation computing systems.

---

GPU 컴파일러 및 AI 워크로드 최적화 (CS598-01)
교과개요
This intensive seminar focuses on the unique challenges of compiling and optimizing applications for Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and other accelerators used in Artificial Intelligence. We will delve into the specifics of GPU architectures, including multi-level memory hierarchies, warp scheduling, and tensor core utilization. The course integrates concepts from graph theory to model computational dependencies and data movement patterns, which are essential for optimizing large-scale deep learning frameworks. Topics include automatic parallelization strategies, kernel fusion techniques, and the development of custom compilers that can handle irregular workloads often found in scientific computing and cryptographic applications like homomorphic encryption. Through hands-on projects, students will implement optimizations that reduce latency and increase throughput by aligning software abstractions with hardware capabilities.
교과목표
Upon completion, students will be equipped to analyze GPU performance bottlenecks and apply advanced compiler transformations such as loop tiling, vectorization, and memory coalescing to achieve near-peak hardware utilization. They will learn to construct domain-specific compilers that abstract away low-level hardware details while exposing sufficient control for fine-grained optimization of AI models. The course also emphasizes the ability to evaluate trade-offs between compilation time and runtime performance, ensuring that generated code is not only fast but also portable across different GPU generations. Ultimately, students will master the skills necessary to build compiler toolchains that enable efficient execution of complex graph-based computations on heterogeneous hardware platforms.

detail.query: Computer architecture / Resource disaggregation / Memory, security / Memory compression / Chiplet에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
컴퓨터 아키텍처 및 리소스 디애그리게이션 (Resource Disaggregation) 에 특화된 가상 강의계획서입니다. 요청하신 형식에 맞춰 작성되었습니다.

컴퓨터구조론 (전산시스템 최적화) (CS450-01)
교과개요
This course explores advanced paradigms in computer architecture with a specific focus on resource disaggregation, memory hierarchy optimization, and security-aware system design. We investigate techniques for decoupling compute, memory, and storage resources to enable flexible scaling and efficient multi-tenant environments. Special emphasis is placed on memory compression algorithms that minimize bandwidth overhead while maintaining data integrity, and the integration of hardware-based security mechanisms within disaggregated architectures. Furthermore, the course examines Chiplet-based design methodologies, analyzing how heterogeneous dies can be interconnected to overcome traditional monolithic scaling limits while addressing inter-chip communication latency and thermal challenges.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design resource-disaggregated system topologies that maximize utilization efficiency under varying workload patterns. Students will master advanced memory compression techniques to extend effective memory capacity without proportional power or bandwidth costs, and implement security protocols tailored for distributed memory pools. Additionally, learners will gain proficiency in evaluating Chiplet interconnect architectures (such as CXL and UCIe) to balance performance, cost, and security trade-offs in next-generation heterogeneous computing systems.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 리소스 디애그리게이션 개요 및 아키텍처 패러다임 전환
2 주차: 메모리 계층 구조와 대역폭 병목 현상 분석
3 주차: 메모리 압축 알고리즘 (Lossless/Lossy) 과 성능 영향도 평가
4 주차: 보안 강화된 분산 메모리 풀 설계 및 접근 제어
5 주차: Chiplet 기반 이종 칩 통합과 인터커넥트 기술 (CXL, UCIe)
6 주차: 이질적 다이 간 통신 지연 최소화 전략
7 주차: 열 관리와 전력 효율성 최적화
8 주차: 실제 사례 연구 - 클라우드 환경에서의 리소스 풀링 구현
9 주차: 보안 취약점 분석 및 하드웨어 기반 방호 기법
10 주차: Chiplet 설계 툴체인과 시뮬레이션 방법론
11 주차: 워크로드 특성에 따른 아키텍처 자동 구성 (Auto-tuning)
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 미래 컴퓨팅 트렌드 논의

detail.query: Data Mining / Query-Aware Data Systems /, Streaming & Adaptive Computation / Applied AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
데이터 마이닝 및 적응형 컴퓨팅 (BS305-01)
교과개요
This course explores advanced techniques for extracting meaningful patterns from high-dimensional and dynamic data streams.
Focusing on the intersection of Data Mining, Query-Aware Data Systems, and Streaming Computation, we examine how
systems can adapt to evolving query workloads in real-time without sacrificing performance or accuracy.
Students will investigate adaptive indexing strategies, online learning algorithms for concept drift detection,
and resource-aware query optimization techniques that leverage hardware heterogeneity. The curriculum bridges
theoretical foundations of statistical learning with practical implementations in distributed environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design scalable data mining pipelines capable of handling
continuous data streams, formulate query-aware system architectures that dynamically adjust to workload changes,
and apply adaptive computation methods to optimize resource utilization in AI-driven applications.
The course also aims to cultivate the ability to evaluate trade-offs between latency, throughput, and model accuracy
in real-world streaming scenarios.

2 주차: Foundations of Query-Aware Data Systems - Workload Modeling and Adaptive Indexing Strategies
3 주차: Sampling Techniques for High-Velocity Streams - Reservoir Sampling and Sketching Algorithms
4 주차: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptation - Statistical Tests and Online Learning Frameworks
5 주차: Anomaly Detection in Streaming Data - Unsupervised Methods and Real-Time Alerting Systems

8 주차: Adaptive Resource Management - Scheduling and Load Balancing for Heterogeneous Clusters

detail.hyde:
Programming Language Foundations for AI (CS598-01)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between traditional programming language theory and the emerging demands of artificial intelligence. We explore how to design, implement, and analyze programming languages specifically tailored for machine learning workflows, such as differentiable programming, automatic differentiation, and tensor computation graphs. The curriculum covers type systems that ensure correctness in neural network code, optimization techniques for large-scale model training, and the integration of symbolic reasoning with deep learning. Students will gain hands-on experience building custom DSLs (Domain Specific Languages) to accelerate research in reinforcement learning, natural language processing, and computer vision.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design programming languages that natively support gradient-based optimization and backpropagation, implement efficient compilers for machine learning frameworks, and formally verify properties of AI models using advanced type theories. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to identify bottlenecks in current ML infrastructure and propose novel language features that enhance scalability, reproducibility, and safety in data-driven applications.

This course explores the design and analysis of systems that must operate within strict timing constraints while interacting with physical environments. Utilizing concepts from Real-Time Systems, Mobile Computing, and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), we examine how to ensure reliability, safety, and determinism in AI-driven services deployed on resource-constrained mobile platforms. The curriculum bridges theoretical scheduling algorithms with practical implementation challenges in heterogeneous networks and edge computing.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to model real-time requirements for cyber-physical applications, design robust architectures for mobile AI services that guarantee temporal constraints, and evaluate trade-offs between computational efficiency and system responsiveness. The course also aims to foster the ability to integrate machine learning models into safety-critical systems without compromising real-time performance guarantees.

detail.query: Cryptography, Distributed Computing, Privacy Enhancing, Technologies에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Privacy-Enhancing Cryptography for Distributed Systems (CSE450)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of advanced cryptography and distributed computing, focusing on techniques that preserve data privacy in decentralized environments. We move beyond traditional encryption to examine protocols such as Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Homomorphic Encryption, and Zero-Knowledge Proofs. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation challenges in large-scale networks, addressing how to perform computations on encrypted data without revealing underlying inputs or intermediate results. Students will analyze the trade-offs between computational efficiency, communication overhead, and security guarantees when deploying privacy-enhancing technologies in real-world distributed architectures.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design cryptographic protocols that enable secure collaboration among untrusted parties in a distributed setting. They will gain proficiency in constructing and evaluating systems based on MPC and Homomorphic Encryption, ensuring robustness against various attack vectors including side-channel analysis and network failures. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to assess privacy risks in emerging distributed frameworks and propose innovative solutions that balance strong security guarantees with practical scalability.

---

Distributed Consensus and Privacy-Preserving Data Analytics (CSE460)
교과개요
This course investigates the fundamental challenges of achieving consensus and performing data analytics in distributed systems where data sensitivity is paramount. We delve into Byzantine fault-tolerant algorithms adapted for privacy constraints, exploring how to maintain system integrity without compromising user confidentiality. Topics include federated learning architectures, differential privacy mechanisms integrated with distributed databases, and secure aggregation protocols for cloud-edge collaboration. Through case studies of blockchain-based identity management and decentralized finance (DeFi) security, students will understand the theoretical underpinnings and practical deployment strategies for privacy-enhancing technologies in next-generation computing infrastructures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate distributed algorithms that satisfy both consistency requirements and strict privacy budgets defined by differential privacy. They will apply secure aggregation techniques to build scalable analytics pipelines that prevent data leakage during model training or query execution. The course also aims to strengthen the ability to critically evaluate the security posture of distributed systems against sophisticated adversaries and communicate complex privacy-preserving design decisions effectively to technical stakeholders.

Analog & Mixed-Signal System Design (EE4XX-01)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between idealized circuit theory and practical silicon implementation, focusing on the design of high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits. We explore the trade-offs between noise, power, speed, and area in real-world environments, moving beyond textbook examples to address challenges in ultra-high-speed data transmission and RF system integration. The curriculum emphasizes a unified view of signal integrity across wireline links and wireless front-ends, preparing students for complex SoC architectures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design robust analog building blocks such as low-noise amplifiers, data converters, and clock recovery circuits that meet stringent specifications for SerDes applications. Students will gain proficiency in modeling non-ideal effects like parasitic capacitance, process variations, and thermal noise, enabling them to optimize ADC/DAC linearity and RFSoC-based programmable digital system performance.

detail.hyde:
RF 시스템 설계 및 에너지 효율 최적화 (EE490-01)
교과개요
This course focuses on the design of energy-efficient Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits (RFICs) tailored for wireless sensor nodes in biomedical and IoT applications. Utilizing advanced analog/mixed-signal techniques, students will explore low-power RF core circuit design, including low-noise amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, and power amplifiers optimized for battery-operated devices. The curriculum bridges theoretical fundamentals with practical constraints such as thermal management, noise figure minimization, and linearity requirements in complex electromagnetic environments. Special attention is given to system-level trade-offs between performance, power consumption, and integration density to enable scalable IoT solutions.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design compact RF front-end circuits that meet stringent energy efficiency targets for biomedical implants and wearable sensors. The course aims to equip students with the skills to select appropriate modulation schemes, implement adaptive power control strategies, and validate designs through simulation and measurement techniques. Furthermore, students will learn to integrate analog/mixed-signal blocks into a cohesive system architecture that maximizes operational lifetime while maintaining reliable communication links in diverse IoT scenarios.

주 2: Fundamentals of Low-Power Analog Circuit Design - Subthreshold Operation and Leakage Control

주 10: Phase-Locked Loops (PLL) and Frequency Synthesis in Battery-Limited Environments
주 11: Antenna Interface Matching and Impedance Tuning for Miniaturized Sensors

주 14: Emerging Trends in Energy Harvesting and Self-Powered RF Nodes

detail.query: Edge-intelligent system, Processing-in-memory circuits, Clock and, data recovery, Mixed-signal circuit design에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design for Edge Intelligence (EE4XX-01)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between traditional analog circuit theory and the emerging demands of edge-intelligent systems. We explore how processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures, high-speed clock and data recovery (CDR), and mixed-signal co-design enable low-power, real-time inference at the device level. Moving beyond idealized models, students will analyze non-idealities in PIM circuits, design robust CDR loops for noisy environments, and integrate analog front-ends with digital logic to create autonomous edge nodes. The curriculum emphasizes practical trade-offs between power, area, and performance in next-generation sensor fusion and IoT applications.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design mixed-signal circuits that support on-chip learning and inference, implement high-speed clock and data recovery mechanisms for asynchronous or low-jitter interfaces, and optimize processing-in-memory architectures for energy-efficient AI workloads. The course aims to cultivate the ability to navigate the complex interplay between analog precision and digital flexibility required for true edge intelligence.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1-2: Introduction to Edge Intelligence and PIM Architectures
- Overview of von Neumann bottleneck vs. Processing-in-Memory paradigms
- Case studies in neuromorphic computing and in-memory compute arrays
- Design challenges specific to low-power edge devices

Week 3-4: Analog Front-Ends for Sensor Fusion
- Transimpedance amplifiers (TIA) for photodiode and MEMS sensors
- Noise analysis and optimization for high-sensitivity applications
- Integration of analog preprocessing with digital signal processing pipelines

Week 5-6: Clock and Data Recovery (CDR) Fundamentals
- Principles of phase-locked loops (PLL) and delay-locked loops (DLL)
- Design of CDR circuits for serial links (e.g., PCIe, USB, Ethernet)
- Jitter tolerance and eye diagram analysis in noisy environments

Week 7-8: Mixed-Signal Circuit Co-Design
- Techniques for simultaneous switching noise mitigation
- ADC/DAC selection and interface design for PIM systems
- Power management circuits for autonomous edge nodes

Week 9-10: Processing-in-Memory Circuit Implementation
- Design of analog multiply-accumulate units within memory cells
- SRAM-based PIM array layout considerations
- Thermal and reliability issues in high-density mixed-signal arrays

Week 11-12: Advanced Topics in Edge AI Hardware
- Event-driven computing architectures (spiking neural networks)
- Hardware acceleration for convolutional neural networks (CNNs)
- Security and privacy implications of edge intelligence circuits

Week 13-14: System-Level Integration and Prototyping
- PCB layout guidelines for mixed-signal high-speed interfaces
- Verification methodologies using simulation and measurement
- Project presentations on proposed edge-intelligent system designs

detail.hyde:
Bio-Integrated Sensor Systems (BIS405)
교과개요
This course explores the design and fabrication of integrated sensing systems that bridge biological interfaces with electronic circuits. Utilizing a multidisciplinary approach combining microfabrication, analog circuit design, and signal processing, students will learn to develop low-power sensor ICs capable of interfacing with physiological signals such as ECG, EEG, and glucose levels. The curriculum emphasizes the unique challenges in biomedical environments, including noise mitigation, biocompatibility considerations, and energy harvesting techniques for implantable devices.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design complete sensor front-end circuits with optimized power consumption suitable for wearable or implantable applications. Students will gain proficiency in modeling biological transducers, implementing differential amplification and filtering stages, and integrating these circuits with microcontroller units for real-time data acquisition. The course aims to foster the ability to translate theoretical circuit concepts into practical biomedical prototypes that meet strict safety and performance standards.

---

Ultra-Low Power Analog IC Design for Energy Harvesting (EE390)
교과개요
This advanced seminar focuses on the architectural and circuit-level design of ultra-low power integrated circuits specifically tailored for battery-free or long-life applications, such as Li-ion battery management systems and autonomous biomedical sensors. The course delves into sub-threshold circuit operation, leakage current minimization techniques, and efficient power management architectures including DC-DC converters and charge pumps. Students will analyze the trade-offs between performance, area, and power in the context of next-generation energy storage interfaces and smart grid monitoring nodes.
교과목표
Students will master the design methodologies for creating high-efficiency power management ICs (PMICs) capable of managing Li-ion battery charging/discharging cycles with minimal overhead. The course aims to equip students with the skills to synthesize custom analog blocks that maximize energy harvesting efficiency and extend device lifetime in resource-constrained environments. Furthermore, participants will learn to validate their designs through SPICE simulation and understand the implications of process variations on low-power analog performance.

This course explores the convergence of advanced materials science, electronics, and biology to develop next-generation wearable and implantable devices. We focus on ultra-flexible electronic systems capable of conforming to complex biological surfaces, integrating additive manufacturing techniques for rapid prototyping of soft circuits, and designing bio-compatible energy harvesting units. The curriculum bridges the gap between traditional rigid silicon electronics and emerging organic/inorganic hybrid materials suitable for intelligent prosthetics and continuous health monitoring.

By the end of this course, students will be able to design and simulate flexible electronic architectures using additive manufacturing principles, select appropriate materials for high-performance energy devices in harsh biological environments, and integrate sensing, processing, and power modules into intelligent prosthetic systems. detail.query: Analog & mixed-signal circuits, Low-power, High-resolution ADC, Brain-computer-interface microsystems, Bio-application AI systems에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Analog Integrated Circuit Design for Bio-Applications (EE450)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between traditional analog circuit design and emerging bio-medical application requirements. We focus on designing low-power, high-resolution mixed-signal circuits specifically tailored for brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and wearable biosensors. The curriculum covers noise analysis in ultra-low signal environments, precision ADC architectures optimized for biological signals, and system-level integration of AI inference engines directly onto the sensor chip. Students will explore trade-offs between power consumption, resolution, and bandwidth critical for implantable or wearable devices.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design mixed-signal front-end circuits capable of extracting micro-volt level neural signals with minimal power dissipation. They will master the implementation of high-resolution successive-approximation register (SAR) and delta-sigma ADCs suitable for bio-potential acquisition. Furthermore, students will learn to integrate simple on-chip AI accelerators for real-time signal processing and demonstrate a complete system design flow from circuit simulation to PCB integration for a prototype BCI microsystem.

---

Bio-Signal Processing and Edge AI Systems (EE465)
교과개요
This course introduces the fundamentals of processing biological signals using advanced digital techniques and artificial intelligence at the edge. We examine the unique characteristics of bio-signals such as EEG, ECG, and EMG, and develop algorithms for denoising, feature extraction, and classification. The emphasis is placed on deploying lightweight AI models (e.g., TinyML) directly onto resource-constrained microsystems used in brain-computer interfaces and implantable medical devices. Topics include quantization-aware training, hardware-efficient neural network architectures, and the co-design of analog front-ends with digital back-ends for optimal system performance.
교과목표
Upon completion, students should be proficient in formulating bio-signal processing pipelines that balance computational efficiency with diagnostic accuracy. They will be able to design and optimize low-power AI inference engines suitable for battery-operated microsystems targeting BCI applications. The course aims to equip students with the skills to translate complex biological data into actionable insights using embedded AI, fostering innovation in next-generation bio-application systems.

Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces and Neural Decoding (BIOE450-01)
교과개요

By the end of this course, students will be able to formulate novel architectures for bio-compatible semiconductor devices, analyze signal-to-noise ratios in noisy biological environments, and design closed-loop control systems for haptic feedback and neural decoding. The course aims to cultivate the ability to translate theoretical concepts of charge transport and electrostatics into practical prototypes for next-generation human-machine interfaces, fostering interdisciplinary innovation in bioelectronics and advanced device engineering.

detail.query: Applied cryptography / Quantum safe cryptography / AI security, / Privacy enhancing technologies / Vehicular security에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자보안 및 차세대 암호학 (CSE501-01)
교과개요
This course explores the paradigm shift in cryptography driven by quantum computing and artificial intelligence. We examine how Shor's algorithm threatens classical public-key infrastructure and investigate post-quantum cryptographic standards developed by NIST. The curriculum integrates privacy-enhancing technologies such as homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation, and differential privacy to address data security in AI-driven environments. Special attention is given to vehicular security architectures, focusing on protecting connected autonomous vehicles from quantum-enabled attacks and ensuring the integrity of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication protocols.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to evaluate the security implications of quantum algorithms on existing cryptographic systems and select appropriate post-quantum algorithms for specific application scenarios. Students will design privacy-preserving machine learning pipelines that maintain data utility while preventing inference attacks, and develop robust security frameworks for vehicular networks capable of resisting both classical and quantum adversarial threats. The course aims to foster the ability to critically analyze trade-offs between computational efficiency, security strength, and implementation complexity in next-generation secure systems.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 컴퓨팅의 암호학적 위협과 포스트-양자 암호 (PQC) 표준 개요
2 주차: 격자 기반 암호와 코드 기반 암호의 수학적 기초 및 구현 분석
3 주차: 다변수 암호와 해시 기반 서명 알고리즘의 성능 평가
4 주차: 동적 환경에서의 PQC 키 관리 및 하이브리드 암호 시스템 설계
5 주차: 호모모픽 암호 (Homomorphic Encryption) 와 프라이버시 강화 기술의 원리
6 주차: 분산 컴퓨팅 환경에서의 안전 다자간 계산 (MPC) 과 차분 프라이버시 적용 사례
7 주차: AI 모델의 보안 취약점 분석 및 양자 내성 머신러닝 기법 탐구
8 주차: 자율주행 차량 네트워크 (VANET) 의 보안 아키텍처와 V2X 통신 보호 전략
9 주차: 양자 키 분배 (QKD) 와 양자 랜덤 넘버 생성기 (QRNG) 의 실용적 한계
10 주차: 차세대 암호 프로토콜의 표준화 과정과 산업 적용 사례 연구
11 주차: 차량 보안 시뮬레이션 및 실제 공격 시나리오 대응 전략 수립
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 양자-고전 하이브리드 보안 시스템 설계

detail.query: Learning over networks, Machine learning theory, Information theory에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
정보이론과 기계학습 이론 (PHY495-01)
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental limits of communication and computation by bridging information theory and machine learning. We examine how concepts such as entropy, mutual information, and channel capacity constrain learning algorithms, while investigating theoretical guarantees for generalization in high-dimensional settings. The curriculum covers rate-distortion theory, minimax lower bounds, and the interplay between model complexity and data efficiency. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, students will understand why certain architectures succeed or fail from an information-theoretic perspective.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to derive fundamental limits for learning tasks using information-theoretic tools, analyze the generalization error of machine learning models via Fano's inequality and similar bounds, and design algorithms that are optimal with respect to sample complexity. The course also aims to equip students with the ability to critically evaluate recent advances in deep learning theory through the lens of information dynamics.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 정보이론의 기초 - 엔트로피와 상호정보량 (Entropy and Mutual Information)
2 주차: 채널 용량과 왜율 정리 (Channel Capacity and Rate-Distortion Theorem)
3 주차: 확률적 학습 모델과 일반화 상한 (Generalization Bounds for Probabilistic Learning Models)
4 주차: 최소최대 하한 (Minimax Lower Bounds) 과 Fano's Inequality
5 주차: 정보이론적 접근을 통한 신경망 표현력 분석 (Analyzing Neural Network Expressivity via Information Theory)
6 주차: 압축 학습과 효율적인 데이터 표현 (Compressed Learning and Efficient Data Representation)
7 주차: 중간고사 및 정보이론적 최적화 문제 풀이 (Midterm Exam and Optimization Problems)
8 주차: 생성 모델의 정보 이론적 해석 (Information-Theoretic Interpretation of Generative Models)
9 주차: 변분 추론과 자유 에너지 원리 (Variational Inference and Free Energy Principle)
10 주차: 네트워크 학습 동역학 및 전파 현상 (Learning Dynamics on Networks and Propagation Phenomena)
11 주차: 대규모 데이터셋에서의 정보 병목 현상 (Information Bottleneck in Large-Scale Datasets)
12 주차: 최근 연구 동향과 미래 전망 (Recent Advances and Future Directions)

detail.query: Distributed AI, Trustworthy AI, On-device AI, Multi-modal AI, Federated Learning에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
분산형 인공지능 및 신뢰성 있는 AI (Distributed & Trustworthy AI)
교과개요
This course explores the architecture and ethical implications of Artificial Intelligence systems operating across decentralized networks. We focus on Federated Learning paradigms to enable model training on edge devices without compromising data privacy, addressing critical challenges in On-device AI such as resource constraints and heterogeneous data distributions. Furthermore, the curriculum integrates Multi-modal AI techniques to enhance system robustness against adversarial attacks, ensuring that distributed models maintain high integrity and trustworthiness in real-world applications.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design efficient Federated Learning protocols for heterogeneous edge environments, implement privacy-preserving mechanisms like differential privacy within multi-modal frameworks, and evaluate the security and reliability of distributed AI systems against various threat models. The course aims to equip learners with the skills to deploy trustworthy AI solutions that balance computational efficiency with rigorous data protection standards.

---

분산형 엣지 컴퓨팅 및 신뢰성 있는 AI (BS305-01)
교과개요
This advanced seminar delves into the intersection of Distributed Systems and Trustworthy AI, specifically targeting the deployment of Multi-modal models on resource-constrained On-device platforms. We examine theoretical foundations for Federated Learning convergence under non-IID data conditions and practical strategies for model compression to facilitate edge inference. The course critically analyzes failure modes in distributed training pipelines and develops methodologies for continuous verification of model fairness and robustness, ensuring that AI systems remain reliable even when operating autonomously across diverse network topologies.
교과목표
Upon completion, students should be proficient in architecting scalable Federated Learning frameworks that support multi-modal data inputs while adhering to strict privacy budgets. They will learn to quantify and mitigate risks associated with model poisoning and inference attacks in distributed settings, ultimately formulating comprehensive strategies for building trustworthy AI ecosystems that seamlessly integrate cloud intelligence with on-device execution capabilities.
